congregational.polity:
Congregationalists hold to congregational polity: the local congregation is a complete church under Christ and governs itself. The members together call their pastor, receive and dismiss members, and oversee their own property and ministry, rather than receiving these decisions from a bishop or a higher court. The bond among members is often expressed as a covenant made before God and one another.

Congregational churches do join together in associations and conferences for fellowship, shared mission and mutual counsel. These bodies advise and support, but they are not understood to rule the local church. The underlying conviction is that Christ is present among the gathered people and that every member has a voice in discerning his will. How much weight regional bodies carry differs from one Congregationalist group to another.
